title: Efficient Microsecond-scale Blind Scheduling with Tiny Quanta
problem: Efficiently handling incoming client requests spawning many very short (microsecond-scale) jobs with high throughput and low tail latency requires blind scheduling with frequent preemption, which current systems do not scalably support.
motivation: Datacenter applications need to handle numerous short-duration jobs with both high throughput and low tail latency to meet performance requirements for user-facing services.
method: TQ preempts jobs—pauses them and switches to another one—at microsecond timescales (millionths of a second). To prevent starvation (a situation where some jobs never get to run), it forces these switches frequently, even if jobs would prefer to keep running. It uses a two-level scheduling hierarchy to avoid bottlenecking: instead of all scheduling decisions flowing through one point, they're distributed across the two levels.
key_novelty: Using forced task switching combined with hierarchical two-level scheduling makes microsecond-scale blind scheduling scalable without creating a scheduling bottleneck.
contributions: TQ system enabling efficient blind scheduling of microsecond-level workloads without prior knowledge of job durations
Novel combination of forced multitasking and two-level scheduling mechanisms
1.2x to 6.8x throughput improvement compared to prior blind scheduling approaches
Maintains low tail latency while achieving high throughput
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract
